alt_text: Canonical median and interquartile-range panels compare measured transportation body-coupling cohorts. Counts and missing values vary by cohort. Fixed rail is shown only as an outlined planned comparator with no numeric value.
finding: Measured transportation cohorts have distinct mechanical and physiological distributions. Passive-passenger environments remain separate from the active-controlled motorcycle context and are not collapsed into one ranking.
functional_meaning: Body coupling preserves the difference between passive vehicle input and active locomotor control while making duration, coverage, and missing modalities auditable.
interpretation: Transportation profiles vary across passive-passenger and active-controlled contexts; sparse modes and missing modalities remain visible.
limitation: This is unequal-n N-of-1 descriptive evidence with modality-specific missingness. No active/passive universal ranking or fixed-rail superiority is inferred.
limitations: Sample counts, date coverage, source scope, missingness, and measurement availability accompany each scientific result.
long_description: Transportation profiles vary across passive-passenger and active-controlled contexts; sparse modes and missing modalities remain visible. SilverRide remains distinct from other sedan/taxi records. Motorcycle remains active controlled and is not interpreted as passive passenger exposure. Fixed rail is a planned, unmeasured comparator and has no numeric bar. N-of-1 case study example This N-of-1 case study example illustrates a review method and is not universal. Canonical case evidence: https://handicapskater.com/evidence/transportation/ Sample counts, date coverage, source scope, missingness, and measurement availability accompany each scientific result.
method_disclosure: This N-of-1 case study example illustrates a review method and is not universal.
